passages.title: Paying for a hotel after a disaster
passages.body: If your home is not safe to live in, FEMA may pay for a hotel or motel for a short time. This is called Transitional Sheltering Assistance. Ask about it when you apply.

passages.title: Help for renters
passages.body: Renters can apply for FEMA help too. FEMA may help pay rent somewhere else while you cannot live at home, and may help replace furniture, clothes and other belongings.

passages.title: Insurance comes first
passages.body: File a claim with your insurance company before you apply. FEMA cannot pay for losses your insurance already covers, but it may help with costs your policy does not cover.

passages.title: The home inspection
passages.body: After you apply, an inspector may call to look at the damage. Inspectors carry a FEMA photo ID badge. An inspector never asks for money.

passages.title: Appealing a decision
passages.body: If FEMA says no, read the letter to learn why. You can appeal in writing. Send a signed letter and papers that answer the reason in the letter.

passages.title: Deadline extended for Missouri storms
passages.body: The deadline to apply for help after the September storms (DR-9901-MO) has been extended. Survivors in the listed counties have more time to register.

passages.title: Pago de hotel después de un desastre
passages.body: Si su casa no es segura, FEMA puede pagar un hotel o motel por un tiempo corto. Pregunte por esta ayuda cuando solicite.

passages.title: Ayuda para inquilinos
passages.body: Los inquilinos también pueden solicitar ayuda de FEMA para pagar alquiler en otro lugar y reemplazar muebles y ropa.
